evidence.quote: let renewalBlock (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : LendingError option =

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The renewability rule (overdue, then limit, then holds, then blocked) now sits in one Tier 2 function, renewalBlock. The existing renew transition and the new loans view both call it. Tier 3 only maps the resulting error to desk text. renew-all attempts Loans.renew and does not re-decide which loans qualify.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The new renewAll function in the Tier 4 presentation module (Lending.Host.Cli) calls the Tier 2 Loans.renew itself. It also loads and saves the store directly and reads the clock, instead of going through a Tier 3 use case. This breaks ARC-BND-01 and ARC-BND-02 and is a new violation. The old inline renew branch did the same, but that was existing code, not a precedent. The new renewedLine also reads Tier 2 Policy.renewLimit from presentation. Nothing effectful happens below Tier 4.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The renewal limit stays a single value, Policy.renewLimit. renewalBlock, the Views reason text and the CLI line all reference it. The 'renewed N of N times' reason is derived from the error's limit field, so it is not a second definition. The blocking rule exists once, in renewalBlock.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-type limit lives in Tier 2 (Policy.renewLimit, used in Loans.renewalBlock), and the 'at limit' decision there is correct. The Tier 4 renewedLine also looks up the member and picks the limit, including a Standard fallback. That re-derives part of the domain rule in presentation. It agrees with Tier 2, so it does not contradict it.

evidence.quote: library.Members |> Map.tryFind loan.Member |> Option.map (fun m -> Policy.renewLimit m.Type)

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds new Tier 4 presentation code that calls the Tier 2 function Policy.renewLimit and reads Tier 1 member data (m.Type) from the library, which breaks ARC-BND-02 and ARC-BND-03. It also threads the full Library into the CLI renderer, which deepens the presentation-to-core coupling. The limit should have come from a Tier 3 view or from the result of Tier 2. The Tier 2 edits themselves (Policy.fs, Loans.fs) are pure and add no effects.

evidence.quote: library.Members |> Map.tryFind loan.Member |> Option.map (fun m -> Policy.renewLimit m.Type) |> Option.defaultValue (Policy.renewLimit Standard)
library.Members |> Map.tryFind loan.Member |> Option.map (fun m -> Policy.renewLimit m.Type)

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The limit values (2, 1 and 4) are defined once, in Policy.renewLimit, and DEC-004 is updated to match. The step that resolves a loan to its borrower's limit, with a Standard fallback, is copied in Loans.renewalBlock and in CommandLine.renewedLine. The two copies agree today but could drift. The limit could instead have been carried in the RenewLimitReached result or in a view.
